A sodden piece of cloth covers the floor beneath the rotten wood table, it appears to be the hide of some great furred beast, but the water has damaged it beyond recognition. Because of the awkward tilting of the tower, much of the water streaming through the rest of the first floor has made its way here. Years of corrosive water has finally worn away the thick stone wall and the water has at last found a way out of the tower via dozens of holes where large stones once were. The water cascades out the holes in a constant stream into a cavern so dark no amount of light seems able to penetrate it.

The area is illuminated.

[Dremsyl's Tower, Dining Room]
The remnants of a beautifully wrought iron chandelier hang from the roof, just above a decayed wooden table. The room is smaller than the main dining room, perhaps the personal dining area of the master of the tower. A sodden piece of cloth covers the floor beneath the rotten wood table, it appears to be the hide of some great furred beast, but the water has damaged it beyond recognition. Because of the awkward tilting of the tower, much of the water streaming through the rest of the first floor has made its way here. Years of corrosive water has finally worn away the thick stone wall and the water has at last found a way out of the tower via dozens of holes where large stones once were. [Dremsyl's Tower, Personal Library]
2 port, door
Rows of tall, thin bookcases run across the walls, containing books filled with lost and forbidden knowledge. A single tome from this collection would no doubt cause any dedicated scholar to turn green with envy. Each manuscript is positioned in its proper place, not a single leaf of parchment out of place. The wizard who once occupied these rooms was a meticulous man, with a desire for order that bordered on the obsessive. This room and its immense font of information must have been one of the ancient wizard's most closely guarded secrets, yet it seemed to easily found.

[Dremsyl's Tower, Dining Room]
The remnants of a beautifully wrought iron chandelier hang from the roof, just above a decayed wooden table. The room is smaller than the main dining room, perhaps the personal dining area of the master of the tower. The tapestries that still hang on the walls reveal in faded color that they were once masterpieces. A sodden piece of cloth covers the floor beneath the rotten wood table, it appears to be the hide of some great furred beast, but the water has damaged it beyond recognition. Because of the awkward tilting of the tower, much of the water streaming through the rest of the first floor has made its way here. Years of corrosive water has finally worn away the thick stone wall and the water has at last found a way out of the tower via dozens of holes where large stones once were.
